subject: Observability POC — success criteria, plan & next steps
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Observability POC — initial recap & success criteria

Hi Marissa / Jordan,

Thanks for the demo earlier today — good discussion. We want to scope a short POC so we can validate Redwood’s observability story against our production needs. High-level goals: validate end-to-end latency, error behavior under load, and the ability to export traces/logs to our observability stack (Datadog/Splunk).

Suggested success criteria from our side:
- P99 end-to-end latency (client -> Redwood -> model -> response) under test workload <= 450ms
- Error rate (5xx + timeouts) < 0.5% over a 24h test window
- Trace sampling and distributed traces exported to Datadog with request-id correlation
- Logs for request/response metadata available in Splunk with at least 30d retention
- Visibility into token consumption and cache hit rates so we can estimate unit costs

Questions for Redwood:
1) Can you provide a concise observability plan for the POC (dashboards, traces, log exports, metrics we should instrument)?
2) What timeline and ownership do you suggest for a 2-3 week POC?
3) Any network / firewall requirements and credentials needed from our side?

We’d like to move quickly — target start the week of Dec 6 if that works. Looping in Priya (product) for technical coordination.

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Head of Integrations, FintechX

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@fintechx.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Observability POC — initial recap & success criteria

Alex — thanks for the clear list and the goals. Really helpful. Below is a proposed observability plan for the POC, timeline, and owners — happy to iterate. I’ve attached a short POC checklist and our network requirements doc (see attachments).

Proposed POC scope (2-3 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): account setup, credentials, sample traffic capture
- Week 1: baseline tests (latency, error under synthetic load), dashboard buildout
- Week 2: integration tests (trace/log export, real traffic sampling), run failure scenarios and cache tuning

POC owners:
- Redwood AE: Marissa Cole — commercial coordination, SOW
- Redwood SE: Jordan Blake — technical lead, observability setup and dashboarding
- FintechX: Alex Rivera / Priya Natarajan — product & infra contacts

Observability plan (what Redwood will deliver and what we’ll ask you to provide):
- Dashboards (Redwood Console) — delivered by Jordan:
  - Request throughput (RPS), success/error rates (4xx/5xx), and retries
  - Latency histograms: p50/p95/p99 for request time and model token generation
  - Token consumption and cost breakdown (tokens per request, batch efficiency)
  - Cache metrics: prefix/KV cache hit rate, cache effectiveness by endpoint
  - Infrastructure metrics: GPU utilization, memory, queue lengths for batching

- Tracing:
  - Redwood will enable distributed tracing and inject request-id headers for correlation
  - We’ll export traces to Datadog (or a provided OTLP endpoint). Default sampling will be 10% with the option to increase for the test window; we’ll also provide targeted sampling for error traces.

- Logs and exports:
  - Structured request/response metadata will be exported to Splunk/your S3 bucket (JSON lines) — includes timestamps, request-id, model, token counts, latency, and error codes
  - Audit logs for deployment/config changes available for 90d in Console (we can extend on request)

- Alerts & regression detection:
  - Baseline alerts: sustained p99 > 450ms, error rate > 0.5% for 15m windows, token cost spike > 30% vs baseline
  - Regression tooling: we’ll run a targeted prompt set and compare quality/latency across model variants and report regressions

Network & access checklist (high level):
- Allowlist Redwood egress IPs (see attached Network-Requirements.pdf)
- Provide a staging API key and example request/traffic profile (size distribution, typical prompt lengths)
- Provide destination (Datadog OTLP) credentials for trace export or a Splunk HEC endpoint

Next steps / milestones:
1) Marissa: send SOW + commercial terms (by EOD Mon) — I’ll include the POC duration and success criteria
2) Jordan: spin up initial dashboards and share read-only links (by Wed)
3) FintechX: provide staging key and network contacts (Priya)
4) Schedule kickoff: propose Dec 6, 10:00 AM PT (60 min) — we can adjust

Attachments: POC-Observability-Checklist.xlsx, Network-Requirements.pdf

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Rivera <alex@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@fintechx.com>, procurement@fintechx.com
Date: 2026-11-27T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Observability POC — initial recap & success criteria

Marissa — this looks good. We’re aligned on the timeline and the proposed success criteria. I’ve looped in procurement (procurement@fintechx.com) — they’ll want an SOW and an estimate for the POC costs. Two quick follow-ups:
- Security/data retention: can you confirm default retention windows for request/response logs and whether log exports can be set to 30d for this POC?
- Audit logs / SOC evidence: procurement may request basic audit log samples — can your team provide an example export?

Thanks — will get Priya to confirm the staging credentials next week.

—Alex

Alex / team — great, glad we’re aligned. Quick updates:
1) I’ll send a draft SOW + POC quote by end of day today and include a short security appendix that covers retention defaults and audit-log examples.
2) Jordan will share read-only dashboard links and the initial trace export configuration by EOD Wed.
3) Confirmed kickoff: Dec 6, 10:00 AM PT — calendar invite coming separately (link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=redwood-fintechx-poc-kickoff).

Audit logs snapshot: happy to provide an example export and minimal SOC evidence (no full report) to support procurement.

If there are specific compliance docs you need (SOC 2 checklist, encryption details), flag them and I’ll loop our Security team.

Thanks — looking forward to kicking off.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
